- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon; apply 1.5–2.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.1–0.5), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently misses high-end of true range (e.g., >70), apply “mean reversion” rule: if 30d true > 70, forecast should not exceed 72 unless sentiment >0.4.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.1) and price is near support, model often fails to anticipate rebound; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture early recovery.
